title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with a mix of startup innovations and government funding initiatives. Meanwhile, the race for satellite supremacy continues as investments reach new heights halfway through the year.

themes.title: Debris Management Innovations
themes.body: A startup collaborating with the University of Texas is making strides in debris trapping technology, which could be a boon for orbital safety. As small debris becomes a growing concern, such innovations may soon be essential for sustainable space operations.

themes.title: Record Satellite Investments
themes.body: Investment in satellite technology is on track to set an annual record by mid-2026, reflecting a robust appetite for connectivity and data services. This surge underscores the increasing reliance on satellite infrastructure across various sectors.

themes.title: Mars Mission Preparations
themes.body: Efforts to lay the groundwork for the first human mission to Mars are gaining momentum, with various stakeholders ramping up their plans. This could signal a new era of interplanetary exploration, albeit one that remains years away.

themes.title: Defense Tech Developments
themes.body: The Defense-Tech IPO window is showing signs of life, with companies like Palantir securing significant contracts. As the military increasingly turns to private sector solutions, expect a flurry of activity in defense-related startups.
